summary: Prepare for CDN and edge engineering roles: HTTP caching, edge configuration on Akamai, troubleshooting live traffic, edge security and automating changes.

topics.title: HTTP caching
topics.why: Most CDN questions come back to what may be cached, for how long, and by whom.
points: Cache keys: what makes two requests the same object

topics.title: Akamai delivery configuration
topics.why: You'll be asked how you would set up and change properties safely.
points: Properties, rules, behaviors and match criteria
Origins, cache keys and TTLs at the edge
Edge logic (EdgeWorkers) and when to use it

topics.title: Troubleshooting delivery
topics.why: Interviewers want a clear method, not guesses.
points: Edge or origin? Reading response headers and debug headers
5xx at the edge, origin timeouts, TLS errors
Hit ratio drops and cache key mistakes

topics.title: Edge security and TLS
topics.why: Most CDN roles include protecting sites at the edge.

topics.title: Configuration as code
topics.why: Safe, repeatable changes are a common interview theme.
points: Review, staging tests and gradual rollout

exercises.title: Explain a cache key
exercises.goal: Show that you can reason about what makes requests cacheable.
steps: Pick a public website and open the browser's developer tools.
Find three responses and note their caching headers.
Decide what you would cache, for how long, and with which cache key.
Record a 3-minute walkthrough with Snazzy Pro: your screen and camera, explaining your choices.

exercises.title: Debug an origin error
exercises.goal: Practise a calm, step-by-step troubleshooting story.
steps: Run a small web server locally that sometimes returns 503.
Use curl with verbose output to show the headers and timings.
Write down how you'd tell an edge problem from an origin problem.
Record a short walkthrough of your method.

exercises.title: CDN change as code
exercises.goal: Build something you can talk about in the automation question.
steps: In your code editor, write a Terraform file for a simple CDN or HTTP config (any provider's sandbox or a mock).
Add a review step and a plan output to your notes.
Record yourself explaining how you'd roll it out and roll it back.

practice.title: CDN Engineer (Akamai)
practice.summary: Practice interview for a CDN engineer working with Akamai: caching and edge configuration, troubleshooting, security and automation.

competencies.name: Caching and edge configuration
competencies.description: Designs caching and edge rules that keep sites fast and correct.

anchors.1: Changes settings without explaining the effect.
anchors.3: Explains a rule they set, why, and how they checked it.
anchors.5: Explains several decisions with trade-offs, testing and measured results.

competencies.name: Troubleshooting
competencies.description: Finds and fixes delivery problems methodically.

anchors.1: Mentions an incident without their steps.
anchors.3: Walks through isolating and fixing a problem.
anchors.5: Walks through a complex incident: isolation, root cause, fix and prevention.

competencies.name: Edge security
competencies.description: Protects sites and origins at the edge.

anchors.1: Mentions security tools only by name.
anchors.3: Describes a protection they set up and why.
anchors.5: Describes balancing protection against false positives, with results.

competencies.name: Automation
competencies.description: Makes changes safe and repeatable with code.

anchors.3: Describes configuration as code with review.
anchors.5: Describes a full pipeline with staging, rollout and rollback.

questions.text: Tell me about a caching rule you designed. What did you decide, and how did you know it worked?
Tell me about a time a website was slow or failing through a CDN. How did you find the cause?
Imagine the cache hit ratio for a site drops from 90% to 40% overnight. What would you check, in what order?
Tell me about a time you protected a site or API from abuse. What did you set up, and what happened?
How would you make CDN configuration changes safe for a team that currently makes them by hand?

practice.company_facts: This is a practice interview. There is no real employer: questions about pay, hours or the team can't be answered here.

settings.next_steps: Your coaching feedback appears as soon as the interview ends.
